summary: Now what we have learned from social scientists and economists like Eleanor Ostrom who are  studying the phenomenon of management of commons on local scale, is that there are certain  prerequisites that you can put into place that enable you to manage an open access  open space for the good of one and all.

Sylvia's wish provides us that leverage, that access to the heart of human beings who  might say who have rarely seen places beyond their own toes but are now hopefully going  to become interested in the full life cycle of creatures like these sea turtles who indeed  spend most of their time in the high seas.

That's this picture doesn't exactly show the plastics that I would like it to show because  I haven't been out there myself but there's just been a study that was released in February  that showed there were 200,000 pieces of plastic per square kilometer now floating  in the surface of Sargasso sea and that is affecting the habitat for the many species  in their juvenile stages who come to the Sargasso sea for its protection and its food.

So what we need to do is to stand up boldly, singling and together  to push governments to push regional fisheries management organizations  to declare our right to declare certain areas off-limits of high seas fishing  so that the freedom to fish no longer means freedom to fish anywhere and anytime.

At the same time, we need to think locally,  which is the joy and marvel of Sylvia's hope spot wish,  is that we can shine a spotlight on many of these previously unknown areas  and to bring people to the table, if you will,  to actually make them feel part of this community  that truly has a stake in the future management.
